articles.title: Astronomers Discover Decagonal Wave circling Saturn’s South Pole | Sci.News
articles.excerpt: For almost five decades, Saturn’s north pole has been famous for hosting a bizarre, six-sided jet stream known as the hexagon, a feature first spotted by NASA’s Voyager spacecraft in the 1980s and still churning today.
articles.content:
For almost five decades, Saturn’s north pole has been famous for hosting a bizarre, six-sided jet stream known as the hexagon, a feature first spotted by NASA’s Voyager spacecraft in the 1980s and still churning today. Astronomers had long wondered whether the ringed planet’s southern hemisphere might hide a mirror-image structure. Now, it turns out the south pole has been quietly growing something of its own: a decagon.

These Hubble images show Saturn and the gas giant’s southern pole with its 10-sided atmospheric wave. Image credit: NASA / ESA / STScI / Agustin Sánchez-Lavega, UPV / Amy Simon, NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center / Michael Wong, UC Berkeley / Alyssa Pagan.

Saturn’s southern hemisphere dropped out of view from Earth in 2012 because of the planet’s axial tilt, and didn’t become observable again until 2023.

When the images captured by the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope in October 2023 were examined, they showed a faint 10-vertex polygon near 63°S.

By August 2024, the shape had sharpened, and by August-September 2025, Hubble and ground-based observers captured all 10 vertices fully formed, though their brightness contrast varied unevenly around the circle.

The observations were taken as part of Hubble’s Outer Planet Atmospheres Legacy (OPAL) program, which has photographed the outer planets annually for more than a decade.

“We’ve never seen anything quite like this in Saturn’s southern hemisphere,” said OPAL principal investigator Dr. Amy Simon, an astronomer at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.

“The northern hexagon has been there every time we’ve looked for more than 40 years.”

“This feature is different — it appears to be strengthening, giving us the rare opportunity to watch a giant atmospheric pattern develop.”

“Given Saturn’s symmetry in its north-south jet stream system, we have been searching for a counterpart to Saturn’s northern hexagon on the south pole in Hubble images since 1990,” said Dr. Agustín Sánchez-Lavega, an astronomer at the University of the Basque Country.

“Images from NASA’s Cassini spacecraft, which orbited Saturn between 2004 and 2017, showed no inkling of a long-lived formation, either. The Hubble data confirmed the feature’s presence back to 2023.”

The decagonal wave sits within one of Saturn’s powerful jet streams and extends through multiple layers of the atmosphere, indicating it is not just a cloud-level feature, but a vertically extended atmospheric structure.

“The most intriguing part to me is that this seems to have just formed recently,” Dr. Simon said.

“The question is, why did it suddenly form now when we haven’t seen one before?”

“Further study is needed from Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope, as well as analysis of computer models, to understand how the decagon formed, how long it may last, and how it compares to the long-lived hexagon in the north.”

A paper about the discovery was published today in the journal Science Advances.

articles.title: UK stresses 'unwavering' position on Falkland Islands ahead of Argentine president's announcement
articles.excerpt: Foreign Office spokesperson tells Anadolu Falkland Islands 'are and will remain a British Overseas Territory, in line with the wishes of the Falkland Islanders' | Anadolu
articles.content:
Reporting the Changing World

Anadolu Ajansı © 2026

Britain has reiterated its "long-standing and unwavering" position on the Falkland Islands, saying they "are and will remain a British Overseas Territory" ahead of Argentine President Javier Milei's planned announcement on the islands.

In a statement to Anadolu, the British Foreign Office reaffirmed that, as minister Uma Kumaran told parliament earlier Wednesday, the UK's position on the Falkland Islands is "long-standing and unwavering."

"They are and will remain a British Overseas Territory, in line with the wishes of the Falkland Islanders," said a spokesperson for the Foreign Office.

The spokesperson added: "The Islanders' right to self-determination is paramount."

It came after President Milei's post on US social media platform X Tuesday, saying he will address Argentina’s "historic claim" to the Falkland Islands in a national broadcast that will be televised at 9 pm local time on Thursday (0000GMT Friday).

Milei claimed what he called "the Malvinas cause" is a historic claim of the Argentine people that to this day "continues to see its national sovereignty violated."

"We will continue defending the interests of the Argentine Nation with tooth and nail, no matter who it bothers," added the president.

Milei's remarks came hours after US President Donald Trump suggested he is reconsidering US support for UK's sovereignty over the Islands, in a move which could strain the "special relationship" between the two countries.

"I always review every position – that’s just one of many," the US president told reporters in the White House on Tuesday.

In 2013, the people of the Falkland Islands voted overwhelmingly in favor of remaining a UK Overseas Territory. Of 1,517 votes cast in the referendum, 1,513 were in favor and three against.

articles.title: Alex de Minaur finally reaches US Open second round amid scheduling backlog
articles.excerpt: Alex de Minaur is up and running at the US Open, Australia’s big title hope finally posting a belated first-round win at Flushing Meadows
articles.content:
• Australia’s No 1 beats Andrea Guerrieri 6-2, 6-2, 6-4 after delays

  • Maya Joint, Daria Kasatkina, Taylah Preston bow out in women’s singles

Australia’s No 1 beats Andrea Guerrieri 6-2, 6-2, 6-4 after delays

Maya Joint, Daria Kasatkina, Taylah Preston bow out in women’s singles

After having his tournament opener against Andrea Guerrieri postponed until day four, Alex de Minaur had to endure another two-hour rain delay before putting away the Italian qualifier in straight sets.

The world No 7 advanced with a 6-2, 6-2, 6-4 victory to set up a second-round clash with Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp.

But Maya Joint was among four Australians to be knocked out of the women’s singles after a 6-2, 6-7 (6), 6-4 defeat to ninth seed Elina Svitolina in the second round.

In a clinical display, De Minaur broke Guerrieri twice in all three sets and only dropped serve once, when he was trying to close out the match at 5-2 in the third.

But New York’s miserable weather has left De Minaur facing a scheduling backlog and needing to win seven best-of-five-set matches in 12 days to lift the trophy.

“These tournaments, it’s all about adapting and that’s the name of the game,” he said.

“There’s too much to play for to let something like this affect you, so I’m glad with the way I handled it. I’m glad I got in and out, played a relatively clean match and now I can focus on the next one.”

The three-times quarter-finalist will need to be back on site on Thursday (Friday AEST) to face the 70th-ranked van de Zandschulp and again the following day if he wins again.

One of the fittest players on tour, De Minaur is backing his supreme conditioning as he faces the prospect of playing three matches in three days.

“It definitely helps to be able to get on the court, get off the court and in straight sets. Every little bit helps.” he said. “Now I’m moving onwards, I’ll be ready for tomorrow. It should be a battle, a physical one.”

When he finally opened his campaign on Wednesday (Thursday AEST), De Minaur looked intent on making up for lost time, racing to a 6-2, 4-2 lead in just 49 minutes before the heavens opened.

After scampering back to the locker room, De Minaur returned to court 11 to wrap up victory in less than an hour.

Joint saved a match point and went on to win the second set in a tie-breaker – the first time the 20-year-old has taken a set off a top-10 opponent – but was unable to keep pace with Svitolina in the third.

The Australian recovered from being 4-1 down in the third set and saved three more match points before Svitolina held her serve to love to move into the next round.

after newsletter promotion

Taylah Preston’s US Open adventure has ended abruptly in the second round. The first Australian through to round two was the first to exit following a 6-1, 6-1 loss to big-hitting American Taylor Townsend.

The 20-year-old wildcard was eliminated in just 48 minutes.

Australian women’s No 1 Daria Kasatkina was also removed from the draw, but not before offering more considerable resistance against Spaniard Paula Badosa.

The pair resumed their stop-start affair that was halted on Wednesday night in sensational fashion.

After first being forced off court because of rain early in the second set, while trailing Badosa 6-1, 1-2, Kasatkina was delighted when officials called it a night immediately after she saved a third match point.

Badosa was furious and had to return 15 hours later trying to serve out the contest at 5-4 and deuce in the second set.

Kasatkina saved her first two match points in an epic 22-point game serving at 3-5 in the second set, before fighting off another six more.

Kasatkina also conjured two break point chances to level up at 5-5 before Badosa, a one-time world No 2, finally closed out the contest to book a second-round date with 2023 champion Coco Gauff.

Kim Birrell also crashed out of the women’s singles in the second round after a 6-1, 2-6, 6-3 loss to Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova.

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones Is Out for Revenge in First Trailer for New Action Thriller Series
articles.excerpt: Jackie Price is out for revenge in the first official trailer for AMC+ thriller series 'Kill Jackie.'
articles.content:
Nothing is getting in the way of Catherine Zeta-Jones as she sets out for revenge in the upcoming AMC+ thriller series, Kill Jackie. In the actor's latest project, Zeta-Jones finds herself fighting off a squad of the world's most ruthless hitmen — The Seven Demons — who suddenly make their mark on her enigmatic character, Jackie Price. Thus, bringing demons (and old criminal instincts) from Price's past roaring up from the depths. AMC+ announced the release date for Kill Jackie last month, but now, audiences are getting an official first look at what the show might have in store, with a new trailer drop released earlier today.

A book-to-screen adaptation based on the acclaimed novel, The Price You Pay, Zeta-Jones stars as an ex-international drug smuggler who has seemingly tried to escape her otherwise dangerous past through lavish living, fine art, and a life of traveling the world. Unfortunately for Jackie, though, it seems no one can truly outrun their past as she soon discovers that someone from her former life is now trying to kill her. Alongside Zeta-Jones, performances from actors like Daniel Ings (A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms​​​​, The Gentlemen series), Enzo Cilenti (Black Mirror, The Crown), and Ron Perlman (Hellboy) are also teased.

Coming from the same brilliant minds that brought us the award-winning series Killing Eve — a four-season thriller that followed the cat-and-mouse infatuation between a spy and MI5 officer — Kill Jackie has the legs to be another intriguing addition to the AMC thriller library — with Zeta-Jones' Jackie Price seen biting people's ears off, blowing up buildings, and fighting off elite assassins with a row of guns hidden beneath her innocuous wall art. These are just a few of the "small misunderstandings" we get to see from Jackie Price's character in the trailer, but it is nevertheless clear that the Seven Demon assassins have picked the wrong woman to mess with.

Prior to her role in Kill Jackie, Zeta-Jones is best known recently for her role as Morticia Addams in the Netflix streaming sensation Wednesday, along with her breakout role as Elena in The Mask of Zorro and her award-winning performance in the musical film Chicago.

The eight-part revenge thriller series, Kill Jackie, will premiere exclusively on AMC+ and is set to launch on Oct. 2 — with new episodes airing weekly. According to a press statement from AMC, Kill Jackie is being co-produced by Fremantle and Steel Springs Pictures and co-created by Conor Keane, Tom Butterworth (Gangs of London), Peter Lawson (John Wick), and Damon Thomas (Killing Eve) — with Thomas also directing.

Iran’s currency hits record low

Iran’s currency, the rial, hit a record low on Wednesday.

Traders in the Tehran market exchanged 2.20 million rials for one US dollar. That was nearly 10% higher than last week’s record, set on August 25, when one dollar was sold at 2.02 million rials.

The currency had already been under pressure before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on February 28 as Iran battled double-digit inflation and negative growth.

The rial has repeatedly hit new lows since the conflict started more than six months ago. The troubled currency ​has lost about half of its value ⁠in a year ​of tightening ​US sanctions ​and American ​and ‌Israeli attacks.

Christou talks about how the latest exchange of strikes are part of a “cycle of escalation” in the tension between the two nations.

Xi’s remarks to his Egyptian counterpart Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, on his first visit to Cairo in a decade, come as Beijing seeks a greater foothold in the region, expanding investment while managing fallout from the six-month conflict.

“We must uphold the principle that the people of the Middle East are the masters of their own affairs, oppose external interference (and) support regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security,” Xi said in a meeting with Sisi, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

articles.excerpt: John Higgins is planning to wind down his snooker schedule as he eyes up retirement in the next two years.
articles.content:
John Higgins is planning to wind down his snooker schedule as he eyes up retirement in the next two years.

The legendary four-time world champion is 51 years old but still competing at the top of the sport, reaching the World Championship semi-finals this year.

The Wizard of Wishaw is ranked number six in the world, but still feels the time to hang up his cue is getting close.

Motivation to practice is low and he expects it to get lower when the practice base he shares with Stephen Maguire and Anthony McGill is no longer used later this year.

‘I think it’s hard to get yourself up for playing. That’s what I feel,’ Higgins told Metro.

‘Even the other boys in the unit, we’re giving that up this year, because they’ve got different things going on as well. Snooker’s maybe not their number one priority when we’re getting older. So, I’ll be going back into the house [to practise], and I think that’s when it could be tough.

‘OK, you’re missing a couple of clutch things, but then when you manage to put a good couple of balls in, it gives you a wee bit of confidence again,’ he said.

‘That’s just what it’s going to be the rest of your career, I think. There’ll be good moments, but there’ll be bad moments as well.

‘But I’ve been a competitor for so many years and people say, “Just go out and enjoy it.” You cannot change who you are. If you’ve been a person who wants to give your all, and you want to go out there and play, it’s very hard to just say, “It’s OK, I don’t mind losing, who cares?” Of course you mind losing! So it’s difficult.’

In a bid to ease himself out of the professional game that he has been playing for 34 years, Higgins will play fewer tournaments than usual over the next two years, starting with missing the English Open next week.

‘I’m not playing in the English, and my thought process now is, I’ll play in so many events and then in the next maybe two years, I’ll just retire.

‘I think it’ll be hard to play a lot of events and then just shut it right off. I think it might help to taper off. If I’m not playing so many events, see how I’m feeling, but I’ll probably take it [retirement] better.

‘I think it’ll be the next couple of years. I think so. Obviously Ronnie says he’s thinking about going around 2028, so I’ll just slip out the back door.’

Ronnie O’Sullivan has indeed suggested 2028 could be the year he retires, believing he has two more good chances at winning an eighth World Championship title.

Higgins still has the drive to compete for snooker’s biggest titles, but he feels it will ebb away soon.

‘It’s tough,’ he said. ‘I don’t want to start coming to tournaments and hating the competing side, because that’s what I’ve always enjoyed.

articles.title: JD Vance says he’s doing ‘God’s work – and if that leads to the end times, OK’
articles.excerpt: Vice-president says on evangelical podcast he would feel ‘not shocked if the antichrist was walking among us’
articles.content:
Vice-president says on evangelical podcast he would feel ‘not shocked if the antichrist was walking among us’

JD Vance has said he is “doing as much of God’s work as possible” and that he is OK “if that leads to the end times”, which he says “are coming”.

The US vice-president made the comments during a Monday podcast interview with Bryce Crawford, a 22-year-old evangelical host with over a million YouTube followers and videos featuring sensationalist headlines including “Preaching the gospel in Chicago’s deadliest neighborhood” and “Debating a ‘gay’ pastor”.

Speaking about the Christian prophetic notion that the world as humanity knows it will end one day, Vance said: “Do I think we are in the end times? I don’t know.

“While I’m fascinated by it, I think that focusing on it too much can be very bad,” he said, adding that if his work “leads to the end times, OK, and if that leads to … us building a better world that thrives and survives for a very long time after I’m gone, that’s great, too”.

Vance, who published a spiritual memoir earlier this summer about his conversion to Catholicism, said: “I think you got to just kinda try and have an attitude of: the end times may be coming, in fact they are coming, it’s just a question of whether they’re coming thousands of years down the road, or a few months down the road.”

He said: “I think there are things about the world that make me feel, like, not shocked if the antichrist was walking among us.”

Vance pointed to artificial intelligence, using the example of an acquaintance who uses AI as a marriage counselor, which he described as “kind of satanic”. He said: “When you completely divorce the human from the social element that God made us for … that’s very bad.”

In response to a question about whether he had ever been in a room that was “spiritually dark”, Vance said he had “been in meetings with world leaders where various issues are being discussed, and somebody will say something or somebody will make an observation, and I’ll feel some darkness about it”.

“It sets off every spiritual alarm bell in my body,” he added.

Vance also defended Donald Trump’s controversial depiction of himself as Jesus in an AI-generated photo, subsequently deleted, that the president posted earlier this year, which Crawford said “made me upset”.

“The president didn’t mean any offense. Obviously, he loves Christians … Did Donald Trump mean to post a meme of himself as God? No. The president has a good sense of humor. He did not mean to mock or mimic God. That’s just not who he is,” Vance said, adding that Trump is “a backslapper” and “a bit of a ball buster”.

Following outrage from Christian supporters, Trump deleted the photo and insisted that the photo was “supposed to be me as a doctor making people feel better”.

articles.excerpt: Saturn, apparently, has been hiding its talents.
articles.content:
Saturn, apparently, has been hiding its talents.

For decades, humanity has puzzled over the gas giant's enormous hexagon swirling around its north pole – a six-sided atmospheric structure unlike anything else known in the Solar System.

Now, it seems, that bizarre feature is not an isolated incident – and Saturn may have a propensity for polygons, rather than a passing whim.

Lurking around the planet's south pole, astronomers led by Agustín Sánchez-Lavega of the University of the Basque Country in Spain have spotted another giant polygon – and this one has ten sides.

"This discovery suggests that the hexagon is not as extraordinary as previously thought and that, in fact, the conditions in Saturn's atmosphere are such that polygonal waves can form in both hemispheres surrounding the polar regions," Sánchez-Lavega told ScienceAlert.

Saturn's most prominent and well-known feature is its magnificent system of icy rings, but the hexagon at its north pole would have to be a pretty close second.

It was first discovered in images from the Voyager probes in 1980 and 1981: a vast, six-sided atmospheric wave swirling around the pole at about 78.5 degrees latitude.

In the intervening decades, both the Hubble Space Telescope and the Cassini-Huygens Saturn probe also captured the strange feature, suggesting that it has remained stable for at least 44 years.

It's a weather phenomenon, but why it has such an almost perfect polygonal shape remains a mystery. And although scientists also thought Saturn's southern subpolar jets might produce a similar feature, none revealed itself across multiple searches.

Then, in 2024, polygon lightning struck for the second time.

In images from amateur astronomers, a dark, undulating line was visible around the planet's south pole.

Work in 2025 confirmed it. While creating polar projections from images of Saturn taken by astronomers Trevor Barry of Broken Hill Observatory in Australia and Jean-Paul Oger of the French Astronomy Association, the team finally saw it: Ten sides, forming an unmistakable polygon around the pole.

High-quality images from the Hubble Space Telescope confirmed it and allowed the team to trace it back to 2023.

"The discovery of the wave really did come as a surprise, as neither earlier images of Saturn taken by the Hubble Space Telescope nor those captured by the Cassini spacecraft whilst orbiting the planet between 2004 and 2017 had shown it," Sánchez-Lavega said.

Centered around 60 degrees south, the decagon appears to be a vast atmospheric wave riding on one of Saturn's powerful eastward jet streams. The jet itself races around the planet at roughly 420 kilometers (260 miles) per hour, while the decagon moves at a comparatively leisurely place of around 10 kilometers per hour.

Like the hexagon, the decagon doesn't appear to be just a pattern sitting across the visible cloud tops. Observations at different wavelengths revealed traces of its shape at different altitudes and latitudes, suggesting a vast, vertically layered structure embedded in Saturn's atmosphere.

Fundamentally, it is the same kind of phenomenon as the hexagon, but – difference in side count notwithstanding – the two polygons are not mirror images of each other.

"In addition to the difference in the number of sides," Sánchez-Lavega explained, "the decagon is situated at a less polar latitude than the hexagon in the southern hemisphere, and is perhaps not as robust, as we have seen that it has formed."

There are so many questions about these differences. Why did the decagon only form a few years ago, compared to decades of stability for the hexagon? Why are their latitudinal positions different?

And why does the southern polygon have ten sides, compared to the north's nature-preferred six?

"It may be linked to the difference in latitude, to the background wind structure, or perhaps even to the presence of a high-pressure vortex at nearby latitudes that could be forcing the formation of the wave," Sánchez-Lavega told ScienceAlert.

There's even a plausible suspect.

Just north of the decagon is a roughly 4,000-kilometer-wide anticyclone – a high-pressure vortex the researchers call a Red Spot – smaller, temporary analogs of Jupiter's famous storm. Intriguingly, the decagon appears most pronounced near the vortex and least distinct on the opposite side of the planet.

The researchers conducted simulations to determine whether this storm – or some other disturbance – could have played a role in the formation of the decagon.

None of their scenarios, however, was able to reproduce the observed decagon exactly.

And, of course, there's this little snag.

"The hypothesis that a nearby anticyclone at that latitude is driving the oscillation is an attractive one," Sánchez-Lavega said. "The same thing happened with the hexagon when it was discovered in 1980, but then the nearby vortex disappeared, and the hexagon remained."

So for now, the answer is tantalizingly out of reach. Currently, the decagon is still there – observing how it changes over the coming months and years could reveal much more about how it formed.

Saturn is tilted on its axis as it orbits the Sun every 29.5 years, giving the planet long seasons lasting about 7.5 years each. Its southern hemisphere is now moving through spring towards summer, tilting increasingly towards the Sun.

Related: Amazing New Photos of Saturn's Moons Have to Be Seen to Be Believed

The increase in solar radiation hitting the southern hemisphere – and the decagon – could cause some interesting changes. And as the south pole tilts further into view, astronomers will have an increasingly good vantage point from which to watch them unfold.

"We need to understand how the decagon evolves – in other words, whether in the coming years it will become unstable and break up, or, conversely, become more stable and robust as solar radiation increases," Sánchez-Lavega said.

Saturn's hexagon has endured for at least 44 years; we only learned of its existence well after it was established.

With the decagon, scientists now have a front-row seat to how Saturn builds its polygons in real time – and whatever happens, it's going to be one heck of a show.

The research has been published in Science Advances.

articles.title: After the flood: human suffering on an unfathomable scale in Nepal’s worst-hit districts
articles.excerpt: Thousands remain missing and aid is hampered by treacherous conditions in communities almost wiped out of existence
articles.content:
Thousands remain missing and aid is hampered by treacherous conditions in communities almost wiped out of existence

Searching for the body of his wife in the mud, Dil Bahadur Shrestha lamented that he did not even have a shovel left. For now, he has been using his hands to try to find her as he picks through the ruins of his house.

On Wednesday morning last week, Jamuna Shrestha, his wife of 50 years, had been at home in Betrawati on the banks of Nepal’s Trishuli River, feeding her beloved chickens and goats.

As deadly flash floods coursed down the river valley, Jamuna was last seen going back into her house, trying to usher her chickens to safety, while others fled uphill. Now that house stands like a muddy carcass, everything inside it destroyed or washed away by the violent force of the water and debris that killed more than 1,200 people in Nepal and Tibet.

Dil Bahadur Shrestha, 70, had been tending to his rice fields and feeding his cows on the opposite bank when he felt the ground tremble and saw a black wave, hundreds of metres high, coming down the valley. He ran to safety in the forest, but not before watching two bridges get swept away behind him. “When it hit, everything was destroyed within two minutes,” he said.

  • Dil Bahadur Shrestha, who is searching for his wife of 50 years, Jamuna.

Dil Bahadur Shrestha, who is searching for his wife of 50 years, Jamuna.

He knows in his heart that his wife is gone, but like thousands caught up in the disaster, her body has yet to be found and she is counted among the missing. More than 5,000 people are reported missing in Nepal and a further 546 in the Tibet region of China.

Rescue workers have still not reached Dil Bahadur Shrestha’s home, so he returned to try to retrieve her body himself. “Maybe she thought the flood wouldn’t reach inside the house,” he said, wiping away tears.

The couple had already rebuilt their home once after an earthquake in 2015 that killed about 9,000 people. As he spoke, his frail body collapsed to the barren, muddy ground where his neighbour’s house once stood.

“Even now, I cannot believe that she is gone,” he said. “I cannot forget her. That’s why I keep walking around looking for her. I still feel as if she might be walking around somewhere here. I keep getting this feeling that she might still be here, looking after the chickens and the goats.”

  • A Rasuwa district sign in the flood debris in Betrawati.

A Rasuwa district sign in the flood debris in Betrawati.

The scale of the tragedy in Betrawati is unfathomable. It was 8.37am when a melting glacier high up in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and Tibet crashed into the valley below, setting off deadly flash floods down Nepal’s Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers. By 8.50am, with only a few minutes’ warning, the settlement of Betrawati was engulfed.

This once-thriving market town was submerged in mud so thick that only the top two floors of a six-storey building are visible. Most houses were washed away entirely or flipped on their sides by the sheer force of the floods. School buses lie overturned. A grocery shop was swept 200 metres from its original location and lies in ruins. The river itself has diverted to a new path that cuts through where the highway once was.

  • An overturned school bus hit by the flood water.

An overturned school bus hit by the flood water.

Fragments of the lives of the thousands who lived here lie scattered in the debris: kettles, teddy bears, a record-keeping book, saucepans, medicine packets, a pair of glasses. At least 250 people are missing, Dil Bahadur Shrestha’s brother and sister-in-law among them.

As Dil Bahadur Shrestha surveyed the ruins of his life, search and rescue teams stood on the opposite bank, looking for the dead. By the end of the day, they had pulled 24 bodies from a single house. A helicopter thundered overhead, white body bags swinging underneath.

“I feel there could still be hundreds of bodies here,” said Dil Bahadur Shrestha. “So many people were swept away all at once, carried off by the raging water.” His voice broke: “Now I’m alone. I am completely alone.”

  • Santamaya Lawat tries to retrieve some of her belongings.

Santamaya Lawat tries to retrieve some of her belongings.

A few metres away, Santamaya Lawat, 57, stood shaking a thick cake of dirt from the few clothes and blankets she had been able to retrieve from her brother’s home, now only partly standing, with a gaping hole in the side. Her own house, built just 10 months ago with her life’s savings, was still so filled with mud she had not yet been able to get inside. Five members of her family are gone.

  • Santamaya Lawat has lost five members of her family as well as her home and her brother’s home next door.

Santamaya Lawat has lost five members of her family as well as her home and her brother’s home next door.

“My heart broke when I came back,” she said. “This was supposed to be the house I lived in for the rest of my life, but everything is gone. It was like heaven here and now it has been turned into hell.”

Further up the river, in the district of Rasuwa, on the border with Tibet, the scale of destruction only gets worse. Many of the villages here were swept away entirely and are only accessibly by army helicopter. Some are still so cut-off and the ground conditions so precarious that the fate of hundreds of people remains unknown. On Tuesday, police search and rescue teams confirmed they had finally been able to begin ground operations in the border village of Timure, recovering 90 bodies so far.

A week after the disaster, survivors who fled up mountainsides were still being collected by army helicopters and evacuated to the army base in Dhunche, Rasuwa district’s administrative headquarters.

The mountain village of Syabru Besi was among those wiped clean away, with even the road to the village gone. According to local government officials, at least 500 people there are missing, a quarter of the population. The village resembles nothing more than a muddy riverbed, just one building left standing.

Chhiring Dorje, a 50-year-old farmer, was among those who managed to escape Syabru Besi, but five of his family are missing. “There were 15 or 16 of us from the village who made it safely to the forest,” said Dorje. “We stayed there for two days before the army came in a helicopter. We had nothing to eat. We survived by drinking water from the forest.”

He stood tightly holding the hand of his nine-year-old granddaughter, Ritu Tamang, who wore a big pink rucksack as they waited at Dhunche army base for a ride down to Kathmandu. Rescue helicopters thundered in and out every few minutes. She said quietly that there was “nothing left where our house used to be. I used to go to school and was in Grade 1. Now the school is gone. There are no teachers either.”

  • Chhiring Dorje, a 50-year-old farmer, was among those who managed to escape Syabru Besi, but five of his family are missing.

Chhiring Dorje, a 50-year-old farmer, was among those who managed to escape Syabru Besi, but five of his family are missing.

  • Chhiring Doreje’s granddaughter Ritu Tamang – waiting to be taken to Kathmandu.

Chhiring Doreje’s granddaughter Ritu Tamang – waiting to be taken to Kathmandu.

With the highways washed away, the only road from Kathmandu to Rasuwa is a perilous unpaved track of mud and stones, weaving through tiny mountain villages. The journey often takes more than 12 hours. The treacherous conditions have made it difficult for aid to reach the worst-hit areas and hindered the rescue and relief operations. Many aid trucks are now stuck in Dhunche, unable to drive further north.

At a small relief camp on the road between Betrawati and Dhunche set up by Nepal’s Dhulikhel hospital, people collected medicine and food supplies. Doctors said dozens of the children here had lost their parents in the floods. More than 200 children from the local Nilakantha school, most aged between five and 11, are also missing, believed to have been washed away as they walked to morning classes.

  • Prakash Nepal, a teacher.

Prakash Nepal, a teacher.

Prakash Nepal, a teacher, said the school had received a warning just 10 minutes before the flood waters hit, when the school bus was already picking up students.

“Luckily, we immediately contacted the bus driver and the vehicle stopped midway so the students were able to survive,” he said. “The surge of water did reach the vehicle, but thankfully it did not cause much damage.”

However, many of the local families had been displaced by the 2015 earthquake and still lived in informal settlements along the riverbank. Most of those children had been walking to school when the flood struck. Prakash Nepal’s eyes welled with tears: “We could not save the students who were still on the road.”

Amid the tragedy, there were also small stories of hope. Sitting on the porch of their village home in Lachyang, Ram Krishna Neupane, 69, and his wife, Muiya Neupane, 66, said their only son had been working as a vet in Syabru Besi when the village was hit.

For two days afterwards they heard nothing and feared he was dead. Then they received a phone call. “He called up from a hospital in Kathmandu; he had been rescued by the army,” said Ram Krishna Neupane. “He could not speak, he was crying so much and we were crying.”

It was, added his wife, “a miracle”.

articles.title: Northampton seek ‘happy medium’ after Hearn claims Pollock worth £1m a year
articles.excerpt: Eddie Hearn is pushing for a seven-figure salary for his client, with Phil Dowson, Northampton’s director of rugby, saying ‘the appetite is for him to stay’ but ‘we have to make decisions based on our budget’
articles.content:
• Player’s representative pushes for seven-figure salary

  • Phil Dowson insists ‘the appetite is for him to stay’

Player’s representative pushes for seven-figure salary

Phil Dowson insists ‘the appetite is for him to stay’

The Northampton director of rugby, Phil Dowson, has said the club “have got to find a happy medium” in contract talks with Henry Pollock after the player’s representative, Eddie Hearn, suggested he should be earning £1m a year.

Pollock is said to earn around £150,000 a season and his current deal expires at the end of the 2026-27 campaign. Hearn has stated Pollock could earn “10 times” that if he were to move to another club, warning “he can’t stay at the club on the money he’s on”.

The 21-year-old has 13 England caps but has made only one start. Hearn says his commercial profile warrants a seven-figure salary. Pollock is among the 25 England players to receive an enhanced contract worth £150,000 and Dowson expressed confidence the Prem champions can keep hold of him.

He said: “It is going well. We are still pushing it through. What Eddie Hearn also said, and people have gone straight to the million-pound remark, but the other thing he said is that Henry wants to win stuff, Henry wants to stay at Saints, Henry wants to play with that group of players. He wants to win the World Cup. I embrace that. I am all for that. The appetite is for him to stay. Now we’ve got to find a happy medium. We really want to keep him, he really wants to stay, and that’s a great start.

“We still have to make decisions based on our budget and our financial situation. We’ll continue to do that in the best way possible. That is in discussion with agents, discussions with the group and discussions with the decision-makers about what we can afford and how we put a squad together, how that fits within our budget.”

Salary cap constraints mean Pollock’s chances of receiving a seven-figure offer are slim, not least because Northampton’s self-imposed budget is significantly less than the cap’s ceiling.

Dowson added: “My job is to try and fit 57, 58 players within a squad on a budget. I’ll continue to do that. Eddie Hearn is great for the game, we want to keep Henry Pollock. Fundamentally, nothing has changed. What he says is based on his job.

“Eddie Hearn has a job to do, and that is to promote his client and ask for more money for his client. He’s doing both of those very effectively. We’ve said we want to publicise and grow the game and he has the ability to do that.”

articles.title: Messy, clever and can barely conceal its rage: is Furious the most outstanding TV show of the year?
articles.excerpt: The story of a serial killer taking revenge on the rich predatory men who abused her just earned a fantastic finale. With career-defining acting, daring Epstein parallels and super dark comedy, it’s a total must-watch
articles.content:
The story of a serial killer taking revenge on the rich predatory men who abused her just earned a fantastic finale. With career-defining acting, daring Epstein parallels and super dark comedy, it’s a total must-watch

You could easily watch the first few minutes of Furious without knowing that it would turn out to be so special. It opens with a scene of pure horror: it’s Halloween night and a real monster is hiding among the pretend ones. A woman we come to know as Catherine Grace (an astonishingly good Lola Petticrew) is inside a man’s house, wearing a creepy kitten mask. The man is in bad shape, crawling on the floor, gasping for air and begging for his life. Catherine is alternately chirpy and tender with him, but eventually, she loses her patience with his pleading. She takes a syringe filled with fentanyl out of a pencil case decorated with sparkly stickers and jewels and finishes the job.

So far, so creepy crime drama, but Furious is already hiding in plain sight, because the monster is not who we think it is. What looks as if it will be a cat-and-mouse story, in which a tenacious FBI agent hunts a twisted serial killer, quickly rips up any expectations. We learn that Catherine was trafficked into sex work as a teenager, and is now making her way through a kill list of predatory and powerful men. Her life has been shaped by a conspiracy of abuse, violence, neglect and indifference. She has decided to take matters into her own broken hands.

The case finds its way to the desk of Alice Black (Emmy Rossum, in the role of her life), a tough former NYPD homicide detective turned recent FBI recruit. Her boss, Nora Washington (an equally excellent Quincy Tyler Bernstine), is the head of the sex crimes and crimes against children unit. She drinks to cope with the horrors she has to witness on a daily basis and is in possession of the darkest sense of humour on TV. She sees the potential, and pain, in Alice, and puts her to work. But as the series progresses, we see what it demands of them both to pursue justice, when they are repeatedly told to step back and stand down.

It is hard to think of a recent drama that has placed quite so much trust in the intelligence of its audience. Every character here is flawed. It has moral ambiguity baked into its core. Alice left the NYPD after being beaten by her cop ex-boyfriend Marshall Connelly (a truly sinister Jake Lacy). She has been ostracised by most of their former colleagues, who either do not believe her or, more likely, do not care. She is suffering from a complex response to trauma, and Furious does not shy away from depicting those complexities. It is a raw and unusually vivid portrait of women and PTSD.

When Alice begins to investigate Catherine and her crimes, Furious becomes a big, bold examination of justice, and what that might look like for women who have no access to it. It can barely conceal its rage, and by the final episode, few would expect it to. Catherine, and countless other young girls like her, have had their lives stolen and destroyed by men who believed themselves to be invincible. “I didn’t get to decide a fucking thing about my life,” she shouts, in one of the series’ most devastating scenes.

There is an obvious timeliness to this story, which may be one of the reasons why it is capable of landing such a blow. The Epstein parallels are not subtle, nor are they intended to be. The rich buy people off to cover up their terrible deeds. They operate in plain sight, daring people to catch them. There is an important photograph of trafficked teenage girls with older, wealthy men. One can only imagine if this show will pop up on the Mountbatten-Windsor streaming queue.

But what Furious provides is a fantasy of power, reclaimed and repurposed for the women who have had it taken away from them, if they ever had it at all. One cop describes Catherine as “five feet tall with her fuckin’ socks on”; that she can overpower her victims is something of a fantasy in itself. The finale has a near-impossible task in that it needs to maintain the bleak spirit of the story, while offering some sort of relief, or reward, for the women we have come to care so much about. It pulls it off by allowing for some magical thinking, while never veering too far from the grim reality of the situation. Some men pay for what they have done, whether formally or off the books. Some are given medals for their criminal behaviour. As messy as it is, the resolution is satisfying enough. Justice was never going to be clean.

Furious is a clever show. It works as a straightforward thriller, gripping and tense, using a murder mystery and a manhunt to expose an institutional conspiracy. It is also an emotionally astute act of catharsis, and this fantasy of revenge can feel, at times, like a much-needed balm. It has been renewed for a second season already. No wonder. It is one of the year’s most outstanding shows, and, after all, there are plenty more monsters out there.

Furious is on Disney+ in the UK and Australia and Hulu in the US

1 min read

A single wavelength of light from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope's Wide Field Camera 3 provides a particularly clear view of the 10-sided atmospheric wave discovered encircling Saturn’s south pole. The feature, labeled “decagon,” is embedded within one of Saturn’s powerful jet streams. The wave is centered around 63 degrees south latitude, and its apparent position shifts slightly depending on the wavelength of light observed. Observations from Hubble at different wavelengths of light reveal the structure at different altitudes. Hubble observations also show that the feature was present as early as 2023 and has become more pronounced over subsequent years.

The “X” and dashed circle in the image represents where data was not captured by Hubble.

articles.content:
Retro gaming fans may want to start making room on their shelves for an upcoming LEGO build that brings a 1990s console back to the spotlight.

Rumors have been swirling for weeks about the next major gaming-themed LEGO release and another leak has arrived with more evidence that a new console build is on the way.

LEGO PLayStation 1 Build Details Leak

The LEGO PlayStation console build has been a poorly kept secret over the last few weeks. Although neither company has officially unveiled the collaboration yet, multiple reliable LEGO leakers have shared key details about the upcoming product.

Videos by VICE

The latest leak came in a series of detailed photos posted to Reddit. The images seem to confirm that the unannounced build is a replica of the PS1 console with a single PS1 controller and multiple hidden easter eggs scattered throughout the build.

According to the leak, this build will be an impressive 1,911 pieces. The leak also suggests that the product will have a recommended retail price tag of $160, which does seem about right for that brick count.

The photos seem to confirm that the build will have a working replica of the flip-up disc tray. Additionally, there will be some hidden builds inside the console that can slide out of the side to reveal more details with references to Ape Escape and Gran Turismo.

In an exciting bit of surprise news, the leaker also claims that there will be an Astrobot gift with purchase available for shoppers who pre-order the PS1 console build while supplies last. The leak did not include any photos of the Astrobot build, so hopefully more details about that will be revealed with the official announcement in the near future.

The leak suggests that the console build is going to release on October 1, which would likely mean an official announcement needs to arrive very soon.

Gaming fans looking for a fix in the meantime can also check out the recently announced new lineup of Nintendo-inspired Mario sets from LEGO. Unlike previous Mario sets that included oversized figured with tech built into them, this new line is more affordable and includes traditional size minifigs and characters.

Be sure to check back soon for more LEGO news and updates.

At this time, the LEGO PS1 build has not officially been revealed and no release date has been shared.

articles.title: A First Look at Michael J. Fox and Harrison Ford’s Next Must-See Project
articles.excerpt: The Shrinking stars have paired up again on a campaign for the Michael J. Fox Foundation.
articles.content:
The Shrinking stars have paired up again on a campaign for the Michael J. Fox Foundation.

Michael J. Fox and Harrison Ford might both be nominated for Emmy Awards for their work on Shrinking, but that isn’t where the collaboration between the two screen legends—who both play characters with Parkinson’s on the hit series—ends. The pair also appear together in a new campaign for the Michael J. Fox Foundation, the 26-year-old nonprofit focused on Parkinson’s, and T&C has a first look here.

The video, which was created by Maximum Effort, the entertainment company helmed by MJFF board member Ryan Reynolds, focuses on the conversations we have around issues like Parkinson’s and what it means to actually offer support to friends and family members experiencing it—which might look different than you’d think.

“As I’ve grown older, I’ve realized social connections mean so much—Parkinson’s or not,” Fox tells T&C. “Shooting Shrinking with Harrison and the friendship we've developed reminded me how important those connections are. I hope the authenticity of our friendship comes through in the campaign. We’re using humor and banter to get at what matters. But there’s tremendous seriousness of purpose behind it. We want the community to know that as long as Parkinson’s exists, the Foundation will be here to support everyone living with the disease. The challenges are real, but knowing you’ve got someone in your corner makes a huge difference. And that’s why this campaign is so important.”

Ford says, “Michael has a remarkable way of making difficult things easier to talk about, and that’s part of what makes working with him and being his friend so special. We wanted to bring some of that honesty and humor to a conversation that a lot of people may not know how to have.”

In addition to his Emmy nomination for his work on Shrinking, Fox will also be honored with this year’s Bob Hope Humanitarian Award, a special accolade previously awarded to Oprah Winfrey, Danny Thomas, George Clooney, Sean Penn, and Ted Danson and Mary Steenburgen. Of course, Fox’s philanthropy is widely known; he was on the cover of T&C’s 2023 November issue in support of his philanthropic work, which stems from the diagnosis he received when he was just 29 years old. For that story, he said, “When I went public, I felt like I stood there naked in the town square and said, ‘Look at me. This is what it is.’ What I didn’t realize was how many other people had been dying to do that.”

In recent years, the foundation had reportedly allocated more money to Parkinson’s research than the U.S. government and as of 2022 was supporting more than $3 billion in research programs—and this new campaign is the next step toward reaching its goals. Debi Brooks, the foundation’s CEO and cofounder, says, “The world has taken notice of the special relationship between Michael and Harrison. Our brand campaign combines humor and compassion to highlight the very serious purpose behind our work. It has been a joy to see these Hollywood giants come together to capture attention and channel it toward what matters most: bringing greater awareness and support to people and families living with Parkinson’s.”

Asked what people can say to a friend, Fox shares this advice: ‘Just saying, ‘I got you, I have your back,and I always will’ means everything. Keep showing up!”

articles.excerpt: The long-rumored LEGO PlayStation set has been confirmed, and it's an impressive recreation of Sony's retro console with a several great Easter eggs.
articles.content:
Keeping it physical.

UPDATE: LEGO has now made the below PlayStation set official, confirming the design and brick count as reported previously. Stand by for pre-orders to go live shortly.

Today's announcement comes as part of the latest showcase from PlayStation. Catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

ORIGINAL STORY: The long-rumored LEGO PlayStation set has been glimpsed in leaked photos, and it's an impressive recreation of Sony's retro console with a several brilliant Easter eggs.

Earlier this year, product listing leaks pointed to a LEGO PlayStation console coming this October. And now, with a month to go, the first photos of the set have hit the internet.

Reliable LEGO source Brick Tap has revealed images of the set's box, as reportedly found in a LEGO store. It's still unclear when LEGO will make the set official, though perhaps we'll hear more tomorrow, during Sony's next State of Play broadcast. That's due to stream online at 9am Eastern, on September 3.

The set itself will reportedly contain 1,911 pieces and come with a pricetag of $160. There will also reportedly be an Astrobot gift with purchase, available while stocks last.

72306 PlayStation first look (via Brick Tap)
by u/BrickTap in Legoleak

While there's no images yet of the Astrobot add-on, the main set's box shows the LEGO console and controller. Printed brick elements perfectly recreate the DualShock's iconic Square, Triangle, Circle and Cross buttons, and the pad can also plug into the console's front.

The console itself includes the PS1's flip-up disc tray, while its sides pull away to reveal miniature scenes from Ape Escape and Gran Turismo. It's a very cool touch, and one that's reminiscent of the Easter eggs found in LEGO's Nintendo range, such as the diorama's hidden in its 1-UP Block set.

It likely won't be long until Sony and LEGO make the set official, and it joins a growing range of retro console builds — such as the Nintendo Entertainment System below. Last month, LEGO also revealed a refreshed range of Super Mario sets, now scaled to feature the first Nintendo minifigures.

articles.title: Football transfer rumours: Jamie Vardy to São Paulo or Sheffield Wednesday?
articles.excerpt: Manchester United targeting defenders? | Liverpool’s move for Malo Gusto rejected? | Chido Obi to Feyenoord?
articles.content:
Today’s fluff is powering down as the nights draw in

Should have, would have, could have. Many fans will be using this phrase today after the Premier League transfer window closed at 11pm last night, meaning no more deals can but made until the winter window opens. Everton will be clawing at the glass like a cat who has seen a pigeon on the grass after a late deal for the USA international Folarin Balogun fell through.

The forward reportedly had his medical with the Toffees, which threw up an issue. Everton then went back to Balogun’s club, Monaco, to renegotiate and an agreement was reached with a deal sheet drawn up. But Balogun then decided against the move. It’s a blow to Everton, who have lost two attacking players this window, with Beto going to Fiorentina and Iliman Ndiaye signing for Manchester City.

Monaco were involved in another big deal that fell through late, on deadline day as Lamine Camara looked likely to join Chelsea. Two initial bids for the Senegal international were rejected but eventually the two clubs agreed a €55m (£47.1m) fee. The 22-year-old had a medical but after Everton came in for Balogun, who Monaco were more happy to sell, the club pulled out of the Camara-to-Chelsea deal. After Balogun to Everton fell through, Monaco could not then sell Camara as they did not sign the deal sheet before the window closed.

There are also whispers that Liverpool contacted Monaco to say they will make a move for Camara in 2027, with the Ligue 1 club perhaps believing that will involve a higher fee than the possible Chelsea deal.

Chelsea also enquired about Spanish midfielder Martin Zubimendi but Arsenal rejected any move for the 27-year-old. The Blues then batted off interest from Liverpool, who wanted to sign the France defender Malo Gusto on loan. Chelsea insisted on a permanent transfer.

Liverpool themselves blocked a deal for Cody Gakpo, who wanted a move to Manchester City. The forward reportedly held talks with Anfield bosses to clear the air after they denied the move.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are already planning a defensive restructure come next summer. It is thought Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Matthijs de Ligt and Lisandro Martínez are all on trial this season and they could potentially be replaced in 2027.

United may lose another player in coming days as Chido Obi wants a loan deal to a club in the Netherlands or Denmark. Both countries’ transfer deadlines are on Wednesday. It is thought Feyenoord are interested in the 18-year-old forward.

Wrexham are interested in Jamie Vardy but they are not the only one keen on the free agent: São Paulo and Sheffield Wednesday also want the 39-year-old. He played for Cremonese last season, and scored seven goals, but the club were relegated from Serie A, prompting the England international’s departure.

With that, our transfer-window watch ends. The Rumour Mill returns in January for plenty of hot gossip in (European) winter. Maybe some of the deals that might have been this summer will come to fruition then?

articles.title: Orange County man recently released in Lake Eola swan killing case accused of metal pipe rampage, police say
articles.excerpt: The man Orlando police say killed a swan at Lake Eola one year ago is back behind bars again, accused of a metal pipe rampage in broad daylight on Monday.
articles.content:
Local News

Police say Adonis Leyva caused property damage during fast food confrontation

ORLANDO, Fla. – The man Orlando police say killed a swan at Lake Eola one year ago is back behind bars again, accused of a metal pipe rampage in broad daylight on Monday.

34-year-old Adonis Leyva is facing felony criminal mischief charges in connection with the incident, which happened along busy East Colonial Drive.

Investigators say he smashed an Arby’s window with the pipe, terrifying one of the female workers there, and then continued to damage nearby property by striking a Dunkin’ Donuts sign.

He is also accused of throwing the pipe at cars while also walking in the roadway.

Leyva was spotted moments later by responding officers at the Wawa across the street, and identified by the Arby’s worker, according to an arrest affidavit.

“I’m glad everybody’s alright,” Kim Long, who was filling up for gas at the Wawa, said. “I hope he gets the help that he needs.”

On Tuesday morning, a worker at a nearby PNC Bank branch noticed that the ATM had been smashed.

Investigators reviewed surveillance footage, which appeared to show Leyva at that location on Monday as well. He faces an additional felony charge for the PNC bank property damage.

News 6 reviewed court records, which show Leyva was arrested nearly a year ago at Lake Eola in a separate, high-profile case involving the killing of a swan.

People at the lake on Tuesday said they have questions about Leyva’s violent, erratic behavior in public places.

“Nobody would feel safe,” Elizabeth Guerrero said. “I don’t think anybody that does cruelty or has harming in their hearts should be free.”

Records also show Leyva went through a mental competency evaluation in that case, and a judge found him fit to stand trial.

Court records indicate he later pleaded no contest and was released less than a month ago after spending 344 days in jail.

News 6 contacted State Attorney Monique Worrell’s office asking whether Leyva received mental health treatment as part of the earlier case and whether he was on probation.

The State Attorney’s Office has not yet answered those questions.

A sign posted at the Arby’s referenced in the police report indicates the restaurant is “no longer open.”
